title: Confined Spaces
whatItIs: A confined space is a place such as a tank, sewer, pit or trench where, because it's enclosed, there's a foreseeable risk from gas, fumes, lack of oxygen, fire or rising liquid.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT enter a confined space if the job can reasonably be done without going in.
If entry is unavoidable, the work MUST follow a safe system of work.
Rescue arrangements MUST be in place before anyone enters or starts work.

keyFacts: Ventilate and test the air before entry, and only go in if it's safe. Keep testing once inside.
If the air can't be made fit to breathe, breathing apparatus is essential.
Never 'sweeten' the air with oxygen: it greatly increases the risk of fire or explosion.

visual.caption: What makes a confined space dangerous (HSE INDG258; HSG150)

items.title: Lack of oxygen
items.text: Rust in steel tanks, some soils, or groundwater on chalk and limestone.

items.title: Poisonous gas, fume or vapour
items.text: Builds up in sewers and manholes; leaks in from contaminated land.

items.title: Liquids and solids
items.text: Can suddenly fill the space, or release gas when disturbed.

items.title: Fire and explosion
items.text: From flammable vapours, or from too much oxygen.

b.label: Less obvious ones
points: Deep excavations, basements, poorly ventilated rooms

onTheTest.question: A workmate collapses at the bottom of a manhole. What should you do?
options: Climb straight in to pull them out
Raise the alarm and follow the rescue plan
Wait to see if they recover
onTheTest.why: HSG150 para 505: many people killed in confined spaces were trying to rescue someone without the right equipment. Use the planned rescue arrangements (CSR reg 5).

onTheTest.question: The air in a confined space can't be made fit to breathe. What must workers wear to go in?
onTheTest.why: HSG150 para 514: if the air can't be made fit to breathe because of a toxic risk or lack of oxygen, workers must wear breathing apparatus.

traps: Untrained rescuers die too: never go in after someone without proper equipment.
An open-topped tank or a deep trench can still be a confined space.
Never use petrol engines inside: the carbon monoxide in their exhaust is too dangerous.
The person outside has a job: keep watch, talk to those inside and raise the alarm.
